items.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
items.content:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.

The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.
The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Ganesh Ananthanarayanan, Matthew Balkwill, Xenofon Foukas, Sanjeev Mehrotra, Bozidar Radunovic, Connor Settle, Ankit Verma, David White, Shawn Cicoria, Mark Martin, Rachel Johnson, Mayur Patel

summaries.zh: 微软研究院研究发现，将AI推理任务从机器人硬件中移出，可提升任务成功率、提高效率，并支持更复杂的物理AI工作负载。这一技术有助于缓解硬件与智能增长的匹配问题，推动现实世界物理AI机器人发展。
summaries.en: Microsoft Research findings demonstrate that offloading AI inference to external hardware enhances task success, improves efficiency, and supports more advanced physical AI workloads in robotics. This approach allows robots to leverage external resources, addressing hardware limitations and enabling smarter, more capable real-world applications.

items.summary: 微软研究院研究发现，将AI推理任务从机器人硬件中移出，可提升任务成功率、提高效率，并支持更复杂的物理AI工作负载。这一技术有助于缓解硬件与智能增长的匹配问题，推动现实世界物理AI机器人发展。

items.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
items.content:
Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules.

The post Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules.
The post Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Felix Pultar, John Gardner, Guoqing Liu, Marwin Segler

summaries.zh: 《Nature》期刊发表的一篇新论文介绍了RetroChimera，一种预测模型，能够加速小分子的化学合成。该模型有助于研究人员大规模探索多种定制分子，从而推动医药、材料和农业领域的进步。RetroChimera通过预测合成路径，显著提高了小分子合成的效率，降低了成本。
summaries.en: The article discusses RetroChimera, a predictive model developed to accelerate small-molecule synthesis. It addresses the slow and costly production of custom molecules for medicine, materials, and agriculture. Published in *Nature*, RetroChimera helps researchers explore diverse molecules by improving synthesis prediction at scale. The model aims to enhance efficiency in chemical synthesis. (99 words)

items.summary: 《Nature》期刊发表的一篇新论文介绍了RetroChimera，一种预测模型，能够加速小分子的化学合成。该模型有助于研究人员大规模探索多种定制分子，从而推动医药、材料和农业领域的进步。RetroChimera通过预测合成路径，显著提高了小分子合成的效率，降低了成本。

items.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
items.content:
What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration.

The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration.
The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Naoto Usuyama, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Tristan Naumann

summaries.zh: GigaPath-Flash和GigaTIME-Flash是高效的病理基础模型，通过降低计算需求同时保持高性能，为大规模研究提供了可能。这些模型有助于更广泛地探索病理学领域，推动群体规模的发现。来源：Microsoft Research。
summaries.en: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash are efficient pathology foundation models that reduce computational demands while maintaining strong performance. These models enable larger studies and broader exploration by cutting costs and resource usage. They represent a significant advancement in pathology research, facilitating population-scale discovery. The innovations are detailed in a Microsoft Research article.

items.title: Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT
items.content:
Skala 1.1, the updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, provides greater accuracy, expanded accessibility across the computational chemistry ecosystem, and a living benchmark to track computational performance.

The post Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT  appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Skala 1.1, the updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, provides greater accuracy, expanded accessibility across the computational chemistry ecosystem, and a living benchmark to track computational performance. 
The post Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT  appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Sebastian Ehlert, Stefano Battaglia, Thijs Vogels, Jan Hermann, Jens Wehner, Giulia Luise, Klaas Giesbertz, Chin-Wei Huang, Aaron Kaplan, Kate Milton, Stephanie Marisa Lanius, Derk Kooi, P. Bernát Szabó, Gregor Simm, Rianne van den Berg, Paola Gori Giorgi

summaries.zh: 微软研究院发布的Skala 1.1深度学习交换关联泛函更新，提高了精度，扩展了计算化学生态系统的可访问性，并作为动态基准来追踪计算性能。该更新有助于加速预测性密度泛函理论的发展。
summaries.en: Skala 1.1, an updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, enhances accuracy and expands accessibility across computational chemistry tools. It serves as a living benchmark to monitor performance, accelerating the development of predictive density functional theory (DFT). The release aims to improve efficiency and usability in computational chemistry.

items.title: MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities
items.content:
A path, a fence, a knot. MindTopo sets a new benchmark for testing how AI understands topological relationships and highlights new opportunities to strengthen spatial reasoning and planning.

The post MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
A path, a fence, a knot. MindTopo sets a new benchmark for testing how AI understands topological relationships and  highlights new opportunities to strengthen spatial reasoning and planning.
The post MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Yunfei Ge, Anbang Liu, Qineng Wang, Johnalbert Garnica, Zihan Wang, Reuben Tan, Jianfeng Gao, Ruohan Zhang, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu, Manling Li

summaries.zh: MindTopo通过测试路径、围栏和结等场景，评估了AI对拓扑关系的理解能力，并确立了新基准。该研究强调，MindTopo为提升AI的空间推理和规划能力提供了新机遇。
summaries.en: MindTopo evaluates the spatial reasoning skills of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by testing their understanding of topological relationships, such as paths, fences, and knots. The results set a new benchmark and highlight potential for improving AI spatial reasoning and planning capabilities. The study was published by Microsoft Research.

items.title: Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement
items.content:
Radiology AI is evolving beyond report generation. CARE-X explores a unified approach that combines flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and measurement-based tools for chest X-ray interpretation.

The post Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Radiology AI is evolving beyond report generation. CARE-X explores a unified approach that combines flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and measurement-based tools for chest X-ray interpretation.
The post Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Mercy Ranjit, Nikhilesh E, Dr. Abhyuday Kumara  Swamy, Tanuja Ganu

summaries.zh: CARE-X是微软研究开发的新型放射学视觉语言模型（VLM），旨在提升胸部X光片解读的临床实用性。该模型整合了灵活推理、校准预测和工具辅助测量技术，并采用辅助监督和奖励对齐学习策略。通过这些创新方法，CARE-X致力于实现更精准、可靠的放射学AI应用。
summaries.en: CARE-X is an advanced radiology AI system designed for chest X-ray interpretation, moving beyond simple report generation. It integrates flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and tool-augmented measurement. The approach combines auxiliary supervision, reward-aligned learning, and specialized tools to enhance clinical utility. This unified method aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of radiology virtual assistants. The system represents Microsoft Research's latest innovation in clinically relevant AI for medical imaging.

items.summary: CARE-X是微软研究开发的新型放射学视觉语言模型（VLM），旨在提升胸部X光片解读的临床实用性。该模型整合了灵活推理、校准预测和工具辅助测量技术，并采用辅助监督和奖励对齐学习策略。通过这些创新方法，CARE-X致力于实现更精准、可靠的放射学AI应用。

items.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI
items.content:
Orchard is an open-source framework for the research community to train and evaluate AI agents across task types. It reduces complexity while supporting strong performance from smaller models by enabling researchers to reuse the same infrastructure.

The post Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Orchard is an open-source framework for the research community to train and evaluate AI agents across task types. It reduces complexity while supporting strong performance from smaller models by enabling researchers to reuse the same infrastructure.
The post Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao

summaries.zh: Orchard是一个开源框架，旨在帮助研究社区训练和评估不同任务类型的AI智能体。该框架简化了操作流程，通过复用基础设施，支持小型模型实现高性能。此框架由微软研究院开发。
summaries.en: Orchard is an open-source framework designed for training and evaluating AI agents across various tasks. It simplifies complexity and enhances performance in smaller models by allowing researchers to reuse infrastructure. The framework aims to support scalable agentic AI research. Developed by Microsoft Research, it provides a unified platform for the community.

items.title: Echoverse: Deep, evolving environments for computer-use agents
items.content:
Computer-use AI agents struggle with multi-step workflows like email and customer support. Echoverse trains agents in realistic environments rather than simply providing more training tasks, helping them improve as the tasks, tests, and environments evolve.

The post Echoverse: Deep, evolving environments for computer-use agents appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Computer-use AI agents struggle with multi-step workflows like email and customer support. Echoverse trains agents in realistic environments rather than simply providing more training tasks, helping them improve as the tasks, tests, and environments evolve.
The post Echoverse: Deep, evolving environments for computer-use agents appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Akshay Nambi, Yash Pandya, Sahil Gupta, Sarthak Harne, Kavyansh Chourasia, Yash Lara, Ahmed Awadallah

summaries.zh: Echoverse是一款用于训练计算机使用型AI代理的深度进化环境。该系统通过模拟真实环境，而非简单增加训练任务，帮助代理提升处理多步骤工作流程（如邮件和客户支持）的能力。随着任务、测试和环境的变化，代理能够持续改进。该技术由微软研究院开发。
summaries.en: Echoverse is a system designed to train computer-use AI agents in realistic, evolving environments. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static training tasks, Echoverse creates dynamic settings where agents can improve through interaction with changing tasks, tests, and environments. This approach helps AI agents better handle complex, multi-step workflows like email and customer support. The system is developed by Microsoft Research.

items.summary: Echoverse是一款用于训练计算机使用型AI代理的深度进化环境。该系统通过模拟真实环境，而非简单增加训练任务，帮助代理提升处理多步骤工作流程（如邮件和客户支持）的能力。随着任务、测试和环境的变化，代理能够持续改进。该技术由微软研究院开发。

items.title: EvoLib: Turning experience into evolving knowledge
items.content:
LLMs do not get smarter just by remembering more. EvoLib turns experience into evolving knowledge, taking reusable skills and insights that help models learn and adapt across tasks long after deployment.

The post EvoLib: Turning experience into evolving knowledge appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
LLMs do not get smarter just by remembering more. EvoLib turns experience into evolving knowledge, taking reusable skills and insights that help models learn and adapt across tasks long after deployment. 
The post EvoLib: Turning experience into evolving knowledge appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Weijia Xu, Zelalem Gero, Michel Galley, Eric Yuan, Jianfeng Gao

summaries.zh: EvoLib是一种技术，能将经验转化为进化知识，帮助大型语言模型在部署后持续学习和适应任务。它通过提取可重用的技能和见解，使模型变得更智能，而不仅仅是记忆更多信息。该技术由微软研究院开发。
summaries.en: EvoLib enhances LLMs by transforming experience into evolving knowledge, enabling reusable skills and insights to support model learning and adaptation post-deployment. It addresses the limitation of LLMs not getting smarter solely through increased memory. The technology facilitates continuous improvement across tasks. The concept was introduced by Microsoft Research.

items.title: Verifying Rust cryptography in SymCrypt, from standards to code
items.content:
Cryptographic code supports vital protections in modern computing systems. Learn how a new method helps verify code as developers write it while preserving speed and adaptability as it gets implemented and evolves.

The post Verifying Rust cryptography in SymCrypt, from standards to code appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Cryptographic code supports vital protections in modern computing systems. Learn how a new method helps verify code as developers write it while preserving speed and adaptability as it gets implemented and evolves.
The post Verifying Rust cryptography in SymCrypt, from standards to code appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Son Ho, Cédric Fournet, Antoine Delignat-Lavaud, Samuel Lee, Jason Fisher, Jessica Krynitsky

summaries.zh: 本文介绍了SymCrypt项目如何通过新方法验证Rust加密代码。该方法在开发过程中验证代码，同时保持实现和演进中的速度与灵活性。文章强调加密代码对现代计算系统的重要性，并展示了Microsoft Research的最新研究成果。
summaries.en: The article discusses a method for verifying Rust cryptography in SymCrypt, focusing on validating code during development while maintaining speed and adaptability. It highlights the importance of cryptographic code in modern computing systems and presents a new approach to ensure security without compromising performance. The method aligns with industry standards and supports evolving implementations. (98 words)
